newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK Pilkington details recovery plans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK Pilkington details recovery plans.

text.p: British glassmaker Pilkington Plc, under severe pressure from the weakness of its European markets, on Thursday announced further details on how it plans to improve group profitability through cost cuts and job losses.
Pilkington said it aims to complete the integration of its automotive glazing businesses, reorganise its European building products activities and significantly reduce overhead costs.
These programmes will lead to job losses and write-offs as a result of significant cost cuts.

"It is too early to be precise in terms of numbers, but the pay back on these programmes is quick and we should be through the major cost impact before March 1998," chairman Nigel Rudd told the company's annual general meeting.
Rudd also said the difficult European trading conditions seen in the second half of last year continued into the first quarter of the current financial year.

While glass prices had increased from the low point seen at the end of March, they remain "relatively subdued". In June, it had said it would increase the price of its glass for building products by eight percent from July 1.
"It's going to be a very tough year trading wise," said Michael Ruby, analyst with Credit Lyonnais Laing. "(But) the expectation is that from this very depressed level, things can only get better".

Pilkington's share price slumped by almost five percent in June after it reported sharply lower annual pre-tax profits of 132 million pounds ($221 million) as a result of low prices and overcapacity in its core European markets.
The share hit a low of 114 pence after the results but have recovered since. At 1230 GMT it stood 1.0 pence lower on the day at 130 on heavy volume.
Pilkington said that as part of the rationalisation of its European automotive glazing business, it was closing its plant in Weisel, northwest Germany, one of its two main plants in that country.
The closure would cut about 400 jobs as part of Pilkington's plans to reduce its European workforce by 20 percent -- over 1,000 people.
The staff reduction plan included over 300 job cuts in Britain and about 120 in Sweden, a spokesman said.
Pilkington said it will also review its European building products business where profits had been "totally inadequate".
The group also aims to significantly reduce overhead costs, which it said totalled 1.0 billion pounds ($1.7 billion), or 30 percent of turnover.
Rudd told shareholders that the appointment in May of Paolo Scaroni as chief executive had given fresh impetus to the drive to boost profitability.

"Overall, 1997/98 will be a year of important transition," said Rudd. "Trading results will continue to be affected by low price levels in Europe but actions we are taking will result in the group entering 1998/99 in much better shape".

It was not only overcapacity in Europe and the collapse in prices, particularly in Germany, that affected Pilkington. The strength of the pound was also a factor, as the UK glass industry has traditionally been subject to European imports.
Analysts forecast pre-tax profits for the 1997/98 year in a wide range either side of this year's 132 million pounds. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
